# Aditya Shukla — AI Engineer & AI Solutions Consultant

> Aditya Shukla is an AI engineer and AI solutions consultant based in Nagpur, India. He builds production-grade agentic AI systems, multi-agent orchestration, LLM and RAG pipelines, voice AI agents and machine learning models for banking and insurance, with guardrails, observability and governance built into every system.

Aditya has 2+ years of experience shipping generative AI to production. He started as a Business Analyst and moved into hands-on engineering across front end, back end and multi-agent orchestration. He owns requirement breakdown, POC development and production rollout, manages the sprint board, leads developers and presents system performance to stakeholders. Client names are confidential.

## Selected work

- Agentic banking assistant: a multi-agent assistant for account operations, beneficiary management and transactions. Aditya architected it end to end, and it is moving to production at a bank. Built with AutoGen, LlamaIndex and FastAPI on local LLMs served with vLLM, with guardrails and Langfuse tracing.
- Banking knowledge assistant (RAG): answers questions from each bank's own documents and policies, with sources. Built with LlamaIndex, ChromaDB, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy and Langfuse. Live in production at four banks (three in India, one international).
- Multi-agent orchestration platform: an internal chatbot that Aditya grew from simple retrieval into an orchestrator with specialist agents for travel planning, competitor intelligence, prospect analysis and research. Built with CrewAI, AutoGen and LangChain.
- Real-time voice and video onboarding agent: a 10-state workflow with OTP verification and document capture, plus compliance-grade outbound calling. Built with Gemini Live API, ElevenLabs, LiveKit and Twilio (SIP).
- Sales copilot for an Indian private-sector bank: lead guidance, objection handling and contextual next-step recommendations, plus RAG-based support over internal knowledge and past cases.
- Logo and hologram validation for an international trade organisation in the UK, using image embeddings and similarity search, plus a maritime query system.
- Predictive ML models: churn prediction for a term insurance plan (moving to production), a customer propensity model and an email triage model.
- Natural-language-to-SQL interfaces for querying structured databases in real time.

## Agent Atlas: a field guide to AI agents

- URL: https://adityabeast12.github.io/port/atlas/
- What it is: an interactive, narrated guide by Aditya that explains how AI agents do real work, safely, for business and technical leaders anywhere in the world.
- Five ideas in order: LLM, RAG, API, tool, agent; and the difference between a workflow and an agent.
- The trick: the model writes a tool call as JSON; code you own validates it, checks permissions and approvals, and makes the real API call.
- The blueprint: three tiers and five layers (channels, a FastAPI gateway, agent orchestration, tools over MCP, data), with tracing, evaluation and an audit trail across all of them.
- Seven working demos on simulated data: an AI voice lead qualifier, CRM lead scoring, quoting, invoice capture with tax-ID and tax checks, cross-system middleware, a permission-aware knowledge assistant (RAG) and automated reporting.
- Regions: every demo switches currency, tax, business-ID checks (GSTIN, EU and UK VAT, EIN, TRN, ABN) and software for India, the EU, the UK, the US, the UAE and Australia.
- The rules, as of November 2026: the EU AI Act (with the Digital Omnibus moving high-risk duties to December 2027), GDPR, the UK Data (Use and Access) Act, US state laws (California, Colorado, Texas) and the federal preemption push, India's DPDP Rules, IT Rules and RBI FREE-AI framework, Canada, Singapore's agentic AI framework, Japan, South Korea, China, Vietnam, Brazil, the UAE and Saudi Arabia, Australia, and the standards ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF and the OWASP Top 10s for LLM and agentic applications.
- Design once: six controls nearly every regime asks for: say it is an AI, keep a person on decisions that matter, explain and allow appeal, label generated content, keep data in-region, keep records and assess risk.
- A 12-minute narrated tour, voiced with an open-source model (Kokoro) running locally, with captions.

## Approach

1. Decompose: break business problems into requirements, data flows and service boundaries.
2. Prototype: build working POCs quickly with Streamlit or React on FastAPI.
3. Orchestrate: connect agents, tools, retrieval and document pipelines into one system.
4. Govern: add guardrails, tracing and model monitoring from day one, so every flow is transparent, debuggable and auditable.
